chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah and others, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) who said:

"Five [types of women] whose husbands may divorce them whenever they wish: the pregnant woman whose pregnancy is evident, the girl who has not yet menstruated, the woman who has ceased menstruating, the one whose husband is absent from her, and the one with whom he has not yet had intercourse."
ai.seo_question: What are the five types of women whose husbands can divorce them at any time according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details five categories of women whose husbands may divorce them at will, exempting them from the standard three-month or four-month waiting periods (*iddah*) prescribed for menstruating women. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the distinct legal status of pre-pubescent girls (*saghirah*), menopausal women (*muqarradah*), and those with absent husbands, emphasizing that the primary purpose of *iddah*—whether for pregnancy confirmation or waiting for potential reconciliation—is absent or altered in these specific cases. The narration underscores the flexibility in marital dissolution when the biological or temporal markers for *iddah* are not applicable.
